study.question: Can moderate item/action width12 with native source-specific interactions, crossed with context width8/16, reduce parameters and measured inference cost while keeping validation click AUC within0.0005 of the unchanged width16 source?
study.hypothesis: The source has a useful middle capacity regime that aggressive halving misses. Native width12 item/action representations can retain more target/history information than width8 while reducing lookups, masked compression, scorer inputs and tower inputs. Narrowing context independently may yield additional storage savings at relatively small quality cost. This is a capacity-allocation hypothesis within the inherited architecture, not a claim of a novel unified architecture or of a new compression mechanism.

nearest_work.difference: Archived exact-version primary text1706.06978v4, lines219-277, inspected: retain candidate-conditioned unnormalized local activation and concatenated field embeddings. This proposal changes source-specific capacity in an existing four-task, action-aware compressed-history adaptation; it does not introduce DIN or reproduce its paper benchmark.

Pinned upstream implementation90bb99a60724e975ec565836266fd86dcad0039d lines55-117 and132-199 confirms per-field embedding_dim, ordered sharing and dict outputs. Use a private architecture-metadata copy to select widths; no changes to fields, vocabularies or host information contracts.

Full source is available in history_g2_r0004_context_only.py and was read with baseline_reference.py. Retain its exact forward/compression/gradient methods. Only constructor capacity metadata and shape calculations change. Native16/16 is the compatibility control.

Earlier group-width code copied context8 coordinates to16 and retained unused maps, so it reduced storage while retaining downstream input widths. Here context8 feeds towers directly, item/action12 feeds scorer and towers directly, and there are no expansion or unused-map modules. Prior source-group factorial motivates but does not establish the proposed middle-width regime.

Earlier native uniform8 reduced latency but lost0.00286509 click AUC against the source. The present factorial uses moderate item12/16 and independently allocated context8/16, rather than another uniform halving.

inherited_components: FeatureEmbeddingDict categorical tables with existing vocabulary, padding and alias identities
Target-conditioned local activation with query/key/difference/product/action inputs, Dice and no softmax
Ten temporal blocks with one uniform and two feedback-stratified summaries per block and count-weighted pooling
Click uniform readout, auxiliary feedback readout, four separate towers and inference reuse of the scorer
Source auxiliary gradient routing and cloned Dice buffers in the functional auxiliary scorer
All host-owned training, information, label, scoring and resource contracts
study.proposed_difference: Use source-specific native widths: context8/16 crossed with item/action12/16. Widths propagate through concatenation, scorer input and tower input without projection, coordinate duplication or unused frozen maps. The private metadata-layout helper preserves ordered sharing, assigns a common maximum width to any cross-source alias group, rejects unsupported encoders/pretraining and never mutates the supplied FeatureMap. Hidden-layer widths, masks, feedback routing and loss are unchanged. The full-width endpoint is a source compatibility control; the other three cells form controlled contrasts around it.
predictions: The native16/16 endpoint should have32060453 total parameters, reproduce the source model state/forward behavior under matched construction and recover source click AUC0.660646940486458 in same-seed host execution. An endpoint mismatch is an implementation issue, not capacity counterevidence.

At least one item12 cell is predicted to have at least15% fewer total parameters than the source, click-AUC delta at least-0.0005, and both model-only batch p50 and p95 at most95% of the contemporaneous native16/16 values. These are prospective screening criteria; they are not observed results or a significance claim.

At fixed context width, item12 should reduce native interaction tensors and scorer input width versus item16. At fixed item width, context8 should reduce tables and tower input width versus context16. Inspect the difference-of-differences for click AUC and latency rather than assuming additive effects.

If native context8/item16 differs from g1-r0011-context8_item16, report this as a change in native readout parameterization/initialization, not as a clean proof that coordinate copying alone caused the difference.

Report all four task AUC/Logloss, auxiliary mean separately, total/embedding/dense parameter counts, host training and allocated GPU time, examples, peak memory, validation wall time, throughput and p50/p95 batch latency. Inherited history-length slices are predeclared; new slices remain exploratory with counts and uncertainty.
falsifiers: Neither item12 cell reaches the predeclared0.0005 click-AUC tolerance while reducing total parameters by at least15%, or an apparent benefit disappears against the relevant native16 item control.
Both item12 cells fail the measured p50 and p95 improvement criterion even if parameter storage shrinks. This would reject the tested inference-cost benefit, not the storage result.

Capacity reductions consistently harm quality across subsequent independent paired seeds, or paired user-cluster uncertainty fails to support practical retention. A single positive seed is insufficient for robust retention.
An advantage depends on extra data exposure, changed masks, labels, loss weights or a modified host recipe: the comparison is inadmissible. Do not repair it by changing frozen contracts.
alternative_explanations: Changing parameter shapes changes random initialization, input fan-in, gradient scale and optimizer trajectories; fixed seed is paired execution, not identical corresponding initial tensors.

This intervention jointly reduces table rank and native interaction width. It cannot attribute any quality change exclusively to storage or to arithmetic; earlier projected-table controls supply only contextual evidence.
Width12 may give less favorable kernel alignment; fewer arithmetic operations do not guarantee lower measured latency.
Cross-source table aliases receive the maximum requested width, potentially reducing nominal savings; actual counts and alias ownership must be measured.

Latency measurements vary with loading and GPU conditions; compare model-only p50/p95 as well as end-to-end inference seconds and repeat measurements through the authorized host interface if consequential.
The context/item split is not parameter-matched because item tables are larger. The factorial estimates group-width effects and interaction, not equal-budget superiority of one semantic group.
Auxiliary performance of the inherited source is substantially below DIN on these labels; click-AUC retention must not be represented as all-task retention or production conversion quality.
